CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL

  (Notice No. N2M21-134)

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the regular meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held
on Monday, November 8, 2021, commencing at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California pursuant to the order of the
Mayor of the City of Alhambra, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal Code, and
Sections 54955 and 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

Consistent with AB 361, the Alhambra City Council meeting will not be physically open to
the public, although the public may participate by video conference or teleconference and
some of the Council Members may choose to participate via video conference or
teleconference rather than attend in person.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and made
a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

Dated:  November 4, 2021
Notice No.  N2M21-134

For those wishing to speak on an agenda or non-agendized item, you have 3 options for participation:

the Mayor. If you do not have access to a computer, please call 626-570-3248 to request public

2) “Raise your hand”: For those members of the public that wish to speak but did not make a request

function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom. Staff will unmute you and announce you

telephone if they would like to speak after asking those on Zoom. Staff will unmute telephone callers
and you may state you wish to speak.
3) Emailed comments to be read into the record: As an alternative to speaking during the meeting,
you can email your comments to the City Clerk at lmyles@cityofalhambra.org by no later than 5:00

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-134

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the regular meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor in accordance with Section 54955 and

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES
Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council
taking action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may
determine that the title has been read.

Recommended Action:  By motion, determine that the titles to all ordinances which appear on
this public agenda have been read, and waive further reading.

CEREMONIALS

1.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: FIRE CHIEF THOMAS M. PHELPS – F2M21-3

  Mayor Lee and the City Council wish to commend and thank Fire Chief Thomas M. Phelps
  for his 41 years of faithful and loyal service to the Fire Department and the City of Alhambra.
  A Certificate of Service plaque will be presented to Chief Phelps for his outstanding work for
  the City.

2.  RECOGNITION FROM THE BREATHE FREE ALHAMBRA COALITION – F2M21-3

  Ms. Guadulesa Rivera, Tobacco Control Program Manager for the Breathe Free Alhambra

  3

   Coalition, will present to the City Council a recognition plaque to honor their leadership and
  action on matters concerning public health and specifically the expansion of smoke-free
  outdoor areas and prevention of youth access to tobacco.

PRESENTATIONS

3.  PRESENTATION AND DISCUSSION REGARDING SB9 (ATKINS) – URBAN LOT SPLITS
  – F2M21-16

  On September 16, 2021, Senate Bill 9 (SB-9), was signed into law by the Governor. SB-9
  amended the California Government Code to allow for urban lot splits. Effective January 1,
  2022, these changes will require local agencies to approve applications to allow property
  owners to split a single-family lot into two lots, add a second home to their lot or split their
  lot into two and place duplexes on each (which would create four housing units on a property
  currently limited to one single-family house). The State’s intent for SB9 is to reduce barriers
  for housing production and increase the supply of affordable housing in the State. Director
  of Community Development Ho will present to the Council a summary and analysis of SB9.

  Recommended Action:  City Council review, receive and discuss the information
  contained in the informational report regarding new State law and urban lot splits under
  Senate Bill 9 (SB9) and provide direction to staff as deemed appropriate.

4.  RESOLUTION TO CAST VOTES FOR REPRESENTATIVE OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  BASIN WATER QUALITY AUTHORITY BOARD - F2M12-46, R2M21-45

  A nomination period was opened to accept nominations for a new San Gabriel Basin
  Water Quality Authority Board Member representing cities with prescriptive pumping
  rights. Robert Gonzales from the City of Azusa and Jorge Marquez from the City of Covina
  were nominated to fill the vacancy. Each City with pumping rights has one vote for each
  10,000 residents or majority thereof, as determined by U.S. Census Data. Alhambra has
  eight votes to be cast. At this time, staff is seeking Council’s direction as to which
  candidate to vote for. The City is required to approve a Resolution to cast these votes and
  submit the Resolution with the ballot no later than December 14, 2021 at 12:00 p.m.

  Recommended Action:  City Council adopt Resolution No. R2M21-45 entitled:
  A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, casting its vote(s)
  for Councilmember  to represent cities with prescriptive pumping rights on
  the Board of the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority casting all eight votes for
  one of the two candidates to represent cities with prescriptive pumping rights on the
  Board of the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority.

 CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 5 – 14)

 All items listed under the Consent Agenda are considered by the City Council to be routine and
 will be enacted by one motion unless a citizen or Council member requests otherwise; in which
 case, the item will be removed for separate consideration.

 5.  NIB: CITYWIDE UTILITY PAVING PROJECT – F2M21-72, N2M21-135

  The City of Alhambra Utilities Department cuts the street surface during the installation
  and repair of the water and sewer systems. These cuts into the asphalt require a
  specialized contractor to perform permanent repair of the street surface. Staff has mapped
  the locations of utility cuts and is seeking a qualified contactor to replace approximately
  9,000 square feet asphalt paving at various individual utility cuts throughout the City. Plans
  and specifications have been prepared; staff has reviewed the plans and found them to
  be consistent with City standards.

  Recommended Action:  City Council approve the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids
  to qualified contractors for the Citywide Utility Paving Project with bids due no later than
  10:30 a.m. on December 9, 2021, and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

6.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF A CONCRETE FORMING TRUCK – F2M21-6A,
  N2M21-119, C2M21-58, M2M21-144

  On September 27, 2021, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting
  Bids for the purchase of one concrete forming truck for the Public Works Division. On
  October 14, 2021 the City Clerk received one bid for the purchase of a Concrete Forming
  Truck for the Public Works Division. The bid received was in the amount of $ 61,780.00.
  The bid received from Advanced Truck Body & Equipment Co., in the amount of
  $61,780.00 is the lowest responsible bid. Staff has reviewed the bid from Advanced Truck
  Body & Equipment Co., and found it is in full compliance and conformance with the bid
  specifications.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Advanced Truck Body & Equipment
  Co. in the amount of $61,780.00 for the purchase of (1) one concrete forming truck; and,
  direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-144)

7.  NIB: CITY YARD PUBLIC WORKS BUILDING ROOFING PROJECT – F2M21-73,
  N2M21-136

  The City Yard Public Works building is a multi-functional facility located at 900 S. New
  Avenue. The building contains offices, fleet maintenance facilities, locker rooms, lunch
  and restroom facilities for the Public Works staff. The steel framed aluminum building was
  constructed in 1970 and has remained largely unchanged since its erection. The roof is
  in need of repair to maintain the buildings integrity and prevent further intrusion of the
  elements. The project bids are due no later than 10:30 a.m. on December 16, 2021 in the
  office of the City Clerk, and will be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Recommended Action:  City Council authorize staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids
  to prospective contractors for the City Yard Public Works Building Roofing Project; and,
  direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  5
11-8-21
 8.  RESOLUTION: AUTHORIZE THE CLOSURE OF THE ALHAMBRA CIVIC CENTER
  LIBRARY FOR HOLIDAYS SCHEDULED – F2M21-16, R2M21-44

  Staff requests that the City Council adopt a resolution authorizing the closure of the
  Alhambra Civic Center Library for holidays scheduled. Alhambra Municipal Code states
  that the City Council must authorize the closure of any city building or facility during regular
  business hours. The Library would like City Council authorization to allow for closure of
  the Alhambra Civic Center Library for the following: Tuesday, December 14, 2021 from
  11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.; Sunday, December 26, 2021; and, Sunday, January 2, 2022.
  There will be no disruption to any essential City services during this proposed closure of
  the Civic Center Library.

  Recommended Action:  City Council adopt Resolution No. R2M21-44 entitled: A
  Resolution of the Alhambra City Council authorizing the closure of the Alhambra Civic
  Center Library

9.  ACCEPT GRANT AMENDMENT: HOMELESS GRANT INCREASE FROM THE SAN
  GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS – F2M20-18, M2M21-145

  On September 9, 2020, the City of Alhambra received notice homelessness grant funds
  from the SGVCOG in the amount of $215,000 were awarded for homeless, services
  including outreach, case management, and emergency housing. A second allocation of
  funds in the amount of $34,000 recently became available as a result of unused funds by
  the regional homeless navigator (Union Station). The City’s HOME Team and the City’s
  homeless services provider (LA CADA) continue to conduct homeless outreach, case
  management and emergency housing services in Alhambra. These activities are eligible
  for reimbursement under the SGVCOG’s additional funds; as such, under a second grant
  Amendment, staff is requesting available grant funds be applied to the City’s ongoing
  homeless support services. An appropriation of funds is needed to enable the City’s
  receipt and expenditure of $34,000 in homeless grant funds.

  Recommended Action:  City Council authorize staff to accept the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments (SGVCOG) grant amendment in the amount of $34,000 for
  homeless outreach, services, and housing navigator continuation; authorize the City
  Manager and City Attorney to sign the Amendment, appropriate the funds; and direct staff
  to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-145)

10.  APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION FOR GRANT APPLICATIONS UNDER THE
  MEASURE A ANNUAL ALLOCATION PROGRAMS – F2M21-18, R2M21-46

  The Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District (RPOSD) is responsible
  for implementing and administering the Los Angeles County Safe, Clean Neighborhood
  Parks and Beaches Measure of 2016 (Measure A) which authorizes dedicated local
  funding for park, recreation, and open space projects and their maintenance through an
  annual special tax on all taxable real property in the County. Staff will submit applications
  to the Measure A Annual Allocation Grant Programs for eligible projects that align with
  City priorities, community input, and park needs assessment. Staff has identified such

  6
11-8-21
   eligible projects as playground replacements and bathroom upgrades at Alhambra Park
  for potential Measure A Annual Allocation applications. In order for the City’s Measure A
  applications to be considered complete, an authorizing resolution from the City must be
  included. The proposed resolution provides blanket authority to proceed with the
  application of projects and receipt of grant funds pursuant to the RPOSD’s policies and
  procedures. Upon approval from the RPOSD on proposed Measure A projects, staff will
  return to the City Council for approval to solicit bids or proposals, appropriate grant funds
  for the proposed projects, and issue notices of completion.

  Recommended Action:  City Council adopt Resolution No. R2M21-46 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California approving the blanket
  authority to file applications for grant funds from the Los Angeles County Regional Park
  and Open Space District for Measure A funding for projects and programs

  225265) in the amount of $854,794.05 for the period ending October 21, 2021; and, Final
  Check List (225266 thru 225374) in the amount of $767,202.79 for the period ending
  October 28, 2021.

14.  RESTRUCTURING OF THE DEPARTMENTS OF PARKS & RECREATION, POLICE
  AND PUBLIC WORKS AND ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE AMENDING
  ORDINANCE NO. O2M21-4789 RELATING TO THE POSITION OF MANAGEMENT
  ANALYST IN THE POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M21-2, O2M21-4794, M2M21-146

  Occasionally, opportunities arise that offer the ability to restructure and reorganize existing

  7
11-8-21
   staffing structures in order to provide for improved operations, functions and customer
  service. Anticipated vacancies in both the Police Department and Community
  Development Department and a vacancy in the Parks and Recreation Department
  provides the opportunity for such restructuring and will produce an overall savings in
  salaries. At the September 27, 2021 meeting, the City Council approved a proposed plan
  for American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 Relief Funds. The plan included a multitude of
  projects relating to the maintenance and repair of City facilities. Following the approval of
  the plan by the City Council, staff recognized a need to centralize the function of building
  maintenance and for a dedicated position to manage the projects and oversee the
  maintenance of all city facilities. The Management Analyst in Public Works will manage
  and oversee projects and maintenance pertaining to all such city facilities.
  Additionally, due to an anticipated vacancy resulting from a retirement within the Police
  Department – Business Division, staff examined the existing administrative staffing
  structure. The current structure included one Administrative Finance Manager who
  oversaw six employees within the Business Division. Upon further reviewing the Business
  Division operations and function of the existing position, staff recommends utilizing a
  Management Analyst instead to oversee and manage all of the business-related functions
  within the Department, such as budgeting, payroll, grants management, contract
  management, and project management.
  Finally, Human Resources staff conducted two recruitments that each time failed to
  produce viable candidates for the position of Deputy Director of Parks and Facilities. Due
  to a lack of qualified candidates and prior weak candidate pools, staff reviewed the existing
  staffing structure and determined that reintroducing the previously vacant and unbudgeted
  Parks Superintendent into the organization will provide the focused skill and expertise
  needed to move a myriad of park related capital improvement projects forward. This
  position will also oversee and supervise parks crews. With the above adjustments to the
  various department staffing structures, the proposed reorganization enables improved
  management and focused operations in each of the aforementioned departments.

  Recommended Action:  City Council, by one motion, take the following actions:

  1.  Approve the restructuring of the Departments of Parks & Recreation, Police and
  Public Works to include one full-time Management Analyst in the Police
  Department, one full-time Management Analyst in the Public Works Department
  and the reintroduction of one full-time Parks Superintendent, and direct staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize the City Council’s action. (M2M21-146);
  and,

  2.  Declare introduced for its first reading the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M21-4794: AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. O2M21-
  4789 RELATING TO THE POSITION OF MANAGEMENT ANALYST IN
  THE POLICE DEPARTMENT

  after which such ordinance shall go into effect immediately upon its
  adoption by a 4/5th vote of the City Council.

PRESENTATIONS

3.  PRESENTATION AND DISCUSSION REGARDING SB9 (ATKINS) – URBAN LOT
  SPLITS – F2M21-16

  On September 16, 2021, Senate Bill 9 (SB-9), was signed into law by the Governor. SB-
  9 amended the California Government Code to allow for urban lot splits. Effective January
  1, 2022, these changes would require local agencies to approve applications to allow
  property owners to split a single-family lot into two lots, add a second home to their lot or
  split their lot into two and place duplexes on each (which would create four housing units
  on a property currently limited to one single-family house). The State’s intent for SB9 was
  to reduce barriers for housing production and increase the supply of affordable housing in
  the State. Director of Community Development Ho presented to the Council a summary
  and analysis of SB9. The presentation is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  Discussion: Councilmember MAZA spoke about concerns surrounding the potential
  affects of SB9 on residential neighborhoods, suggested ordinances which would restrict
  SB9 as much as possible, and made a motion to draft an ordinance incorporating elements
  listed in presentation to preserve residential neighborhoods.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER disagreed with the assessment that Alhambra is a

  2
11-8-21
   high public transit corridor and that therefore the parking allotment could be reduced for
  new housing projects because residents could make use of public transportation. She
  stated that while Valley Boulevard and Atlantic Boulevard were high transit with the most
  reliable public transportation lines, that the rest of the City did not have the same access
  and that extra parking was necessary due to families owning multiple vehicles. She went
  on to request that staff provide options for SB9 regulations which would provide for
  moderate income housing as well as low-income housing to better accommodate first time
  homebuyers and families. She stressed the need for strict lot size and height
  requirements. She requested that staff return with a presentation of potential options
  where the City could better regulate SB9 for its own specific needs.

  Councilmember PÉREZ expressed her concerns that restricting SB9 may conflict with the
  City’s goals to streamline the ADU application process and policies. Ms. PÉREZ and Mr.
  HO continued to discuss the background of state legislature regarding ADUs, the evolution
  of local government response to that legislature, and the potential of SB9 to follow a similar
  trend. They went on to discuss the differences between SB9 and previous legislation. Ms.
  PÉREZ stated that she supported LEED certification but added that it might incur
  additional costs which would make it prohibitive to some residents. She added that there
  were concerns regarding single family zoning and its inherent racist roots. She stated that
  she supported heigh restrictions and historic neighborhoods in Alhambra. Ms. PÉREZ and
  Mr. HO went on to discuss the differences between nominally historic neighborhoods in
  Alhambra and official process to designate historic neighborhoods and properties through
  ordinance and state regulation.

  Councilmember MALONEY recognized the pressure legislation such as SB9 puts on local
  governments as it takes away discretion to plan for their own development future and also
  recognized the ongoing housing crisis in California and the Los Angeles area that the State

  ordinances passed by other cities.

  Mayor LEE echoed previous comments and discussed the reaction of residents and local
  government leaders. She discussed the misassumption that property value in R1
  neighborhoods indicates high income, explaining that there were many senior citizens who
  purchased their homes many years ago and can neither afford to move or change their

  affected by design guidelines and historic preservation programs. Ms. LEE also discussed
  the requirement that property owners reside on site for three years after an approved lot
  split.

  AND PUBLIC WORKS AND ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE AMENDING
  ORDINANCE NO. O2M21-4789 RELATING TO THE POSITION OF MANAGEMENT
  ANALYST IN THE POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M21-2, O2M21-4794, M2M21-146

  8
11-8-21
   Occasionally, opportunities arise that offer the ability to restructure and reorganize existing
  staffing structures in order to provide for improved operations, functions and customer
  service. Anticipated vacancies in both the Police Department and Community
  Development Department and a vacancy in the Parks and Recreation Department
  provided the opportunity for such restructuring and would produce an overall savings in
  salaries. At the September 27, 2021 meeting, the City Council approved a proposed plan
  for American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 Relief Funds. The plan included a multitude of
  projects relating to the maintenance and repair of City facilities. Following the approval of
  the plan by the City Council, staff recognized a need to centralize the function of building
  maintenance and for a dedicated position to manage the projects and oversee the
  maintenance of all city facilities. The Management Analyst in Public Works would manage
  and oversee projects and maintenance pertaining to all such city facilities.

  Additionally, due to an anticipated vacancy resulting from a retirement within the Police
  Department – Business Division, staff examined the existing administrative staffing
  structure. The current structure included one Administrative Finance Manager who
  oversaw six employees within the Business Division. Upon further reviewing the Business
  Division operations and function of the existing position, staff recommended utilizing a
  Management Analyst instead to oversee and manage all of the business-related functions
  within the Department, such as budgeting, payroll, grants management, contract
  management, and project management.

  Finally, Human Resources staff conducted two recruitments that each time failed to
  produce viable candidates for the position of Deputy Director of Parks and Facilities. Due
  to a lack of qualified candidates and prior weak candidate pools, staff reviewed the existing
  staffing structure and determined that reintroducing the previously vacant and unbudgeted
  Parks Superintendent into the organization would provide the focused skill and expertise
  needed to move a myriad of park related capital improvement projects forward. This
  position would also oversee and supervise parks crews. With the above adjustments to
  the various department staffing structures, the proposed reorganization enables improved
  management and focused operations in each of the aforementioned departments.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions:

  1.  Approved the restructuring of the Departments of Parks & Recreation,
  Police and Public Works to include one full-time Management Analyst in
  the Police Department, one full-time Management Analyst in the Public
  Works Department and the reintroduction of one full-time Parks
  Superintendent, and directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the City Council’s action. (M2M21-146); and,

  2.  Declared introduced for its first reading the following ordinance entitled:
